headline: Seshaasai Technologies Limited: Intimation of Acquisition/Purchase of Immovable Property
sum: **Seshaasai Technologies disclosed acquisition or purchase of immovable property** under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR 2015, filing a general update with the NSE.
implication: Material Event disclosure under Reg 30 LODR signals property acquisition may cross monetary or strategic thresholds requiring exchange notification; review the full Regulation 30(4) exemption analysis and whether independent valuation was obtained.
detail: Seshaasai Technologies Limited, listed on NSE, intimated the exchange of an acquisition or purchase of immovable property on 25 August 2026. The intimation was filed under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, which requires listed companies to disclose material events and information to the stock exchange. The specific acquisition value, location, intended use and any related-party status were not disclosed in the publicly available regulation-30 notice header; the full PDF attachment would contain the substantive details and any valuation support.

framework.note: Mandates timely disclosure of material events; immovable property acquisition may be 'material' based on value or strategic impact; exemptions in Reg 30(4) apply for routine transactions below prescribed thresholds or in ordinary course of business.
Requires submission of financial results; any large acquisition may trigger contingent liability or asset-valuation disclosures in quarterly/annual filings.
Director approval required for acquisition or sale of immovable property beyond prescribed limits; may require shareholder consent depending on value and Related Party status.
If acquisition involves a Related Party (director, key managerial personnel, relative), prior Board and shareholder approval needed under RPT framework.
If immovable property received for consideration below fair market value, excess value may be taxable income to recipient.
Immovable property transfer requires stamp duty payment and registration under the applicable state's Registration Act; vary by state and property type.
If acquisition is related-party transaction and above threshold, requires independent director committee review and shareholder approval.

conditions: Compliance with Regulation 30 LODR disclosure requirement
Likely Board approval under Companies Act 2013, Section 180 (if above prescribed limits)
Possible Related Party Committee and shareholder approval if transaction involves director, KMP or relative
approvals: Shareholder approval if RPT and above threshold (Section 188 CA 2013)
structure.novel: No novel structuring indicated; standard listed-company real estate acquisition with mandatory Regulation 30 disclosure.

triggers.note: Material event disclosure requirement triggered; company must file intimation within prescribed time (typically 24 hours of intimation to board).
Property acquisition above prescribed limit triggers director approval; value not disclosed, so applicability cannot be confirmed.
State-specific stamp duty and registration laws apply on transfer of immovable property; costs and timing vary by location.
